{{More footnotes|date=October 2016}}
'''Sauro Succi''' is an Italian [[scientist]], internationally credited for being one of the founders of the [[Lattice Boltzmann]] method for [[fluid dynamics]] and [[soft matter]].<ref>{{Cite book |title=The Lattice Boltzmann Equation - for fluid dynamics and beyond| publisher=Clarendon Press| year=2001| last1=Succi| first1=Sauro}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |  title= The Lattice Boltzmann Equation - for complex states of flowing matter| publisher=Oxford University Press| year=2018| last1=Succi| first1=Sauro}}</ref>

== Life and career ==
Succi was born in [[Forlì]].<ref name="cv2020">{{cite web |url=https://www.fondazionecariforli.it/downloads/files/CV%20Succi%20Sauro.pdf |title=CV Succi Sauro |work=fondazionecariforli.it |date=2020-01-22 |language=it |access-date=2025-04-04}}</ref> In 1979 he obtained a degree in nuclear engineering at the [[University of Bologna]], from 1981 to 1982 he was Euratom fellow at the [[Max-Planck-Institut für Plasmaphysik|Max Plack Institute for plasma physics]] in [[Garching]], and in 1987 a PhD in physics from the [[EPFL|Ecole Polytechnique Federale de Lausanne]]. From 1986 to 1995 he worked as a research scientist at the IBM European Center for Scientific and Engineering Computing in [[Rome]].<ref name="CV-IIT">{{cite web |url=https://drive.google.com/file/d/1O_S9p5-oeb3UUvrHfk1-zDsE9_u-LIkN/view |title=Curriculum Vitae |date=2024 |access-date=2025-04-04}}</ref>

From 1995 to 2018, Succi has been research director at the Istituto Applicazioni Calcolo of the [[Consiglio Nazionale delle Ricerche|National Research Council]] (CNR) in Rome.<ref>{{Cite web | url=http://www.iac.rm.cnr.it/~succi/ |title = Sauro Succi's CNR Home Page}}</ref><ref name="CV-IIT"/> Since 2018, he has been appointed principal investigator of the research line Mesoscale Simulations at the Italian Institute of Technology (IIT).<ref name="iit">{{Cite web | url=https://www.iit.it/people/sauro-succi |title = IIT People - Sauro Succi}}</ref><ref name="CV-IIT"/>

He is also a research affiliate to the Physics Department at [[Harvard University]] (since 2000), Fellow of the [[Freiburg Institute for Advanced Studies]] (FRIAS) and senior fellow of the [[Erwin Schrödinger International Institute for Mathematical Physics]].

He has published extensively in [[plasma physics]], [[fluid dynamics]], [[Phonons|kinetic theory]], [[quantum fluids]] and [[soft matter]].{{cn|date=July 2025}}

Succi has been holding visiting/teaching appointments at many academic Institutions, such as the University of [[Harvard]], [[Paris VI]], [[University of Chicago]], [[Yale]], [[Tufts]], [[Queen Mary, University of London|Queen Mary]] London, [[Scuola Normale Superiore]] di Pisa and the Swiss Polytechnic of Zürich ([[ETHZ]]).

From 2014 to 2019 he has been a Visiting Faculty at the IACS ([[Institute of Applied Computational Science]] of [[Harvard University]]), where he taught Computational Methods for the Physical Sciences (AM227).{{cn|date=July 2025}}

== Honors and awards ==
Succi is an elected Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]] (1998). He has received the [[Humboldt Prize]] in physics (2002), the [[Killam Award]] bestowed by the [[University of Calgary]] (2005) and the [[Raman Chair]] of the [[Indian Academy of Sciences]] (2011), he is co-recipient of the Honorable Mention award of the 2011 Gordon Bell Prize and the ''[[Sigillum Magnum]]'' of the [[University of Bologna]] (2018). He also served as an external senior fellow at the [[Freiburg Institute for Advanced Studies]] (2009–2013), senior fellow of the [[Erwin Schrödinger International Institute for Mathematical Physics]] in Vienna (2013) and Weston Chair at the [[Weizmann Institute of Science]] in Rehovot (2016) and External Faculty Member of the [[Institute for Advanced Studies of Amsterdam]] (2017), Visiting Scientist at the IHES Paris (2024). In 2022 he has been appointed [[Honorary Professor at University College London]].<ref name="iit"/> Associate Member of the Higgs Center for Theoretical Physics, University of Edinburgh (2025-2028).

Succi is an elected member of the [[Academia Europaea]] (2015), and he features in the list of Top Italian Scientists.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://topitalianscientists.org/tis/3114/Sauro_Succi_-_Top_Italian_Scientist_in_Physics |title=Sauro Succi |work=topitalianscientists.org |access-date=2025-04-04}}</ref>

He has been awarded the 2017 [[American Physical Society|APS]] [[Aneesur Rahman Prize for Computational Physics]].

In 2017 he has been awarded the [[European Research Council#Advanced Grants|ERC Advanced Grant]] "Computational design of porous mesoscale materials (COPMAT)" and in 2024 the ERC-Proof-of-Concept grant LBFAST (Lattice Boltzmann For Advanced SimulaTions).<ref name="iit"/>

In 2019 he was awarded the Berni J. Alder CECAM Prize for "''having transformed the [[Lattice-Boltzmann method]] into an overarching framework for kinetic physical phenomena. In addition, he has been pivotal in building and constantly inspiring a community now counting tens of thousands of researchers in academia and industry, all across chemistry and physics, and reaching into more distant fields such as engineering or biology''".<ref>{{cite web |url=https://cecam50.cecam.org/berni-alder-prize/ |title=Winners of the Berni J. Alder CECAM Prize |access-date=2025-04-04}}</ref>

He is the co-recipient of the Premio Aspen Institute Italia 2024 for excellent collaboration between Italy and the USA<ref>[https://www.aspeninstitute.it/premio-aspen-2024-la-ricerca-vincitric Premio Aspen 2024]</ref> and the recipient of the 2023 Eugenio Beltrami Senior Scientist Prize for the Mathematics and Mechanics of Complex Systems.<ref>[http://memocscenter.univaq.it/memocs/en/attivita/the-eugenio-beltrami-senior-scientist-prize/ Eugenio Beltrami Senior Scientist Prize]</ref>
2025 he received Visioni Prize for Science and Research, Confindustria Romagna.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.confindustriaromagna.it/media/editor_files/28-10-24_visioni_-_innovare_oltre_gli_orizzonti_-_30_ottobre_teatro_bonci__cesena_.pdf |title=I VISIONARI 2025 |language=it |website=confindustriaromagna.it |access-date=2026-05-15}}</ref>
